readout.retrieval_query: Design an original cooperative game for six strangers using paper, string, and twelve tokens. Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Setup  
Six players sit in a circle. Each receives two tokens. A single loop of string is placed in the center; the twelve tokens start beside it.

Turn order  
Players take turns clockwise. On your turn you must either (1) tie one of your tokens onto the string loop or (2) untie one token already on the loop and keep it.

Shared objective  
Create one closed string shape that holds exactly twelve tokens.

End condition  
When every token is on the string and the loop is closed without gaps, the group wins.

Possible failure  
If at any moment three or more players have no tokens left, the game ends in failure.

Recovery rule  
Any player may, once per game on their turn, give one of their tokens to any other player instead of tying or untying.

readout.retrieval_query: Design an original cooperative game for six strangers using paper, string, and twelve tokens. Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Setup: Six players sit in a circle. Each receives two tokens. A single loop of string lies in the center; twelve tokens start beside it.

Turn order: Starting with the tallest player and moving clockwise, each player on their turn either (1) places one token on the string or (2) ties a new overhand knot somewhere on the string, sliding any tokens already on that segment so none rest on a knot.

Shared objective: Form a closed loop of string whose total length (measured in hand-spans) equals the number of tokens placed on it.

End condition: The loop is closed and its length matches the token count; all players then succeed together.

Possible failure: After every token is placed, the measured length still differs from the token count.

Recovery rule: Any player may, once per game and instead of a normal turn, untie one knot, returning its segment to smooth string; play then resumes with the next player.

Build a closed “web” by connecting every player’s wrists with the string while placing all twelve tokens on the knots.

Any player may spend one token to loosen the nearest knot, letting the group adjust the loop without ending the turn.

Setup  
Six players sit in a circle. Each receives two tokens. A single loop of string is placed in the center; the twelve tokens start beside it.

Players take turns clockwise. On your turn, place one token inside the loop and either (a) pass the string to the neighbor on your left or (b) tie a simple overhand knot anywhere on the string. You must keep at least one token in reserve until the final round.

Any player may spend their last token to “mend”: retie the broken knot immediately, but the next player skips their turn.

readout.retrieval_query: Design an original cooperative game for six strangers using paper, string, and twelve tokens. Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Setup  
Six players sit in a circle. Each receives two tokens. A single loop of string lies in the center; twelve tokens start beside it.

Turn order  
Players take turns clockwise. On your turn, place one token on the string or move one already placed. You may speak one sentence about a value you want the group to share.

Shared objective  
Build a closed shape on the floor with the string that encloses all twelve tokens.

End condition  
The shape is closed and contains every token; all players then say “closed.”

Failure  
If three consecutive turns pass with no tokens added or moved, the game ends unfinished.

Recovery rule  
Any player may spend their remaining token to restart the turn order, letting everyone place one extra token before normal turns resume.

readout.retrieval_query: Design an original cooperative game for six strangers using paper, string, and twelve tokens. Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Setup  
Six players sit in a circle. Each receives two tokens. A single loop of string lies in the center; twelve tokens start beside it.

Turn order  
Players take turns clockwise. On your turn, place one token on the string or move one already on it one finger-width along the loop. You may also give one of your tokens to any other player.

Shared objective  
Fill the entire string with tokens so every segment between players holds exactly two tokens.

End condition  
The game ends when the string is full or any player has no tokens left on their turn.

Possible failure  
If a player cannot place or move a token because none remain in their possession, the group fails.

Recovery rule  
Any player may, once per game, return one personal token to the center pool so the player who would otherwise be stuck can continue.

readout.retrieval_query: Design an original cooperative game for six strangers using paper, string, and twelve tokens. Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Setup  
Six players sit in a circle. Each receives two tokens. A single loop of string is placed in the center; twelve tokens start beside it.

Turn order  
Players take turns clockwise. On your turn, tie one loop of string around one of your tokens and pass both to the player on your left. That player may keep or trade the token for one of theirs.

Shared objective  
Create one closed chain of exactly twelve tokens linked by string loops.

End condition  
The chain is complete when twelve tokens are connected in a single loop and every player holds zero tokens.

Possible failure  
If any player still holds tokens after the string runs out, the chain cannot close.

Recovery rule  
Any player may, once per game, cut their current loop of string, freeing one token to be immediately re-offered to the group.

readout.retrieval_query: Design an original cooperative game for six strangers using paper, string, and twelve tokens. Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Setup  
Six players sit in a circle. Each receives two tokens. A single loop of string lies in the center; twelve tokens start beside it.

Turn order  
On your turn, place one token on the string or move one already on it one hand-span clockwise. Then pass the string to the player on your left.

Shared objective  
Create one closed loop of string that carries exactly twelve tokens.

End condition  
The loop is closed and holds twelve tokens; all players have used both of their tokens.

Possible failure  
If any player has no tokens left while fewer than twelve are on the string, the game ends in failure.

Recovery rule  
Any player may give one of their remaining tokens to a neighbor who has none, but only once per game.

readout.retrieval_query: Design an original cooperative game for six strangers using paper, string, and twelve tokens. Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Setup  
Six players sit in a circle. Each receives two tokens. A single loop of string is placed in the center; players may hold or pass it.

Turn order  
Players act clockwise. On your turn, you must either (1) place one token on the string to “anchor” it or (2) move the string one hand-width clockwise to any player who still holds a token.

Shared objective  
Create a closed, stable loop of string supported by at least six tokens (one per player) without letting the loop collapse to the table.

End condition  
The loop stays elevated for three full clockwise rounds after the sixth token is placed.

Possible failure  
If the string touches the table before the end condition, the game ends in collapse.

Recovery rule  
Any player may spend their remaining token to “knot” two adjacent segments of string together, instantly lifting the loop back to hand height; play then resumes with the next player.

readout.retrieval_query: Design an original cooperative game for six strangers using paper, string, and twelve tokens. Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Setup  
Six players sit in a circle. Each receives two tokens. A single loop of string lies in the center; twelve tokens start beside it.

Turn order  
Players take turns clockwise. On your turn, place one token on the string or move one already on it one finger-width along the loop. You may also pass your second token to any neighbor.

Shared objective  
Fill the entire loop with tokens so none of the string shows between them.

End condition  
The loop is completely covered or three consecutive turns pass with no tokens added.

Failure  
If the loop is still incomplete when three turns elapse without additions, the group fails.

Recovery rule  
Any player may spend both remaining tokens to “reset”: remove three tokens from anywhere on the loop and immediately take an extra turn.

readout.retrieval_query: Design an original cooperative game for six strangers using paper, string, and twelve tokens. Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Setup  
Six players sit in a circle. Each receives two tokens. A single loop of string lies in the center; twelve tokens start beside it.

Turn order  
Players take turns clockwise. On your turn, place one token on the string or move one already on it one finger-width along the loop. You may also pass your second token to any neighbor.

Shared objective  
Fill the entire string with tokens so every segment between players holds exactly two tokens.

End condition  
When the string is full and each gap shows two tokens, the group wins.

Possible failure  
If any player runs out of tokens before the string is full, the game ends in loss.

Recovery rule  
Once per game, any player may spend their turn returning one token from the string to any player who has zero, resetting that player’s count to one.

readout.retrieval_query: Design an original cooperative game for six strangers using paper, string, and twelve tokens. Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Setup  
Six players sit in a circle. Each receives two tokens. A single loop of string is placed in the center; the twelve tokens start beside it.

Turn order  
Players take turns clockwise. On your turn you must either (1) tie one of your tokens onto the string with a simple overhand knot or (2) pass one token to any neighbor who has fewer than two.

Shared objective  
Create one continuous string circle that holds all twelve tokens and can be lifted off the table without any token slipping.

End condition  
The game ends when the circle is lifted successfully or when any player has zero tokens left and cannot receive one on their turn.

Possible failure  
If the string breaks under tension or a token falls during the lift, the group fails.

Recovery rule  
After a failure, each player may give one token to any other player; play then resumes with the next clockwise turn, attempting a new lift.

readout.retrieval_query: Design an original cooperative game for six strangers using paper, string, and twelve tokens. Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Setup  
Six players sit in a circle. Each receives two tokens. A single loop of string lies in the center; twelve tokens start beside it.

Turn order  
Players take turns clockwise. On your turn, place one token on the string or move one already on it one “step” (hand-width) along the loop. You may also pass your second token to any neighbor.

Shared objective  
Fill every hand-width of the loop with at least one token before the tokens run out.

End condition  
When no tokens remain outside the loop, count gaps. Zero gaps = success; any gap = failure.

Failure  
If gaps remain, the circle “breaks.” All players lose unless the recovery rule is used.

Recovery rule  
Once, at any time, the group may vote to cut the string at one gap, tie the ends together to shrink the loop, and redistribute any displaced tokens evenly. Play then resumes; if gaps persist after redistribution, the game ends in loss.

readout.retrieval_query: Design an original cooperative game for six strangers using paper, string, and twelve tokens. Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Setup  
Six players sit in a circle. Each receives two tokens. Place the remaining six tokens in the center as a shared “bridge” pile. One long string forms a loose loop around the circle; each player holds a segment.

Turn order  
Players act simultaneously each round:  
1. Whisper one true, supportive statement to the neighbor on your left while gently tugging the string once.  
2. If the statement is met with a nod, slide one of your tokens into the bridge pile.  
3. If anyone has no tokens left, the round ends.

Shared objective  
Grow the bridge pile to twelve tokens, symbolizing a stronger, united community.

End condition  
The game ends when the bridge pile reaches twelve tokens or when any player has zero tokens and cannot contribute.

Possible failure  
If the pile has fewer than twelve tokens when a player runs out, the group has “lost connection.”

Recovery rule  
Any player may give one token to a neighbor who has none, but must also retell that neighbor’s earlier supportive statement to keep the circle strong.

response:
Setup  
Six players sit in a circle. Each receives two tokens. A single loop of string is placed in the center; the twelve tokens start beside it.

Turn order  
On your turn, tie one new knot in the string or move one token onto an existing knot. Then pass the string clockwise.

Shared objective  
Weave the string into a single closed net that can hold all twelve tokens without any falling through.

End condition  
The game ends when every token rests on a knot and the string forms one unbroken loop.

Failure  
If the string is pulled taut into a straight line or any token drops, the group fails.

Recovery rule  
Any player may spend their turn untying one knot to reposition a fallen token, but the group then loses one token permanently.

readout.retrieval_query: Design an original cooperative game for six strangers using paper, string, and twelve tokens. Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Setup  
Six players sit in a circle. Each receives two tokens. A single loop of string is placed in the center; twelve tokens start beside it.

Turn order  
Players take turns clockwise. On your turn, tie one new knot in the string and move one token from your hand onto any existing knot (including the new one). You may also give one token to any other player.

Shared objective  
Weave the string into a single connected web that touches every player’s seat. All twelve tokens must rest on knots.

End condition  
The game ends when either the web reaches every seat and all tokens are placed, or the string runs out of usable length (agreed by any two players).

Possible failure  
If three or more tokens lie on the floor at any time, the web collapses and the group loses.

Recovery rule  
Once per game, any player may spend their turn to pick up two fallen tokens and immediately tie them together with a new overhand knot, returning them to play.

readout.retrieval_query: Design an original cooperative game for six strangers using paper, string, and twelve tokens. Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Setup  
Six players sit in a circle. Each receives two tokens. A single loop of string is placed in the center; twelve tokens start beside it.

Turn order  
Players take turns clockwise. On your turn, place one token on the string or move one already on it one finger-width along the loop. You may also pass your second token to any neighbor.

Shared objective  
Form a closed “bridge” of exactly twelve tokens spaced evenly around the loop so every player can reach any token by sliding a finger along the string without lifting it.

End condition  
The bridge is complete when twelve tokens sit evenly spaced and every player silently signals agreement by placing both hands palms-up on their knees.

Possible failure  
If any token falls off or spacing becomes visibly uneven before twelve tokens are placed, the round ends immediately.

Recovery rule  
Any player may spend their turn retrieving one fallen token and returning it to the center pile, but the group then loses one token permanently from the total needed.

readout.retrieval_query: Design an original cooperative game for six strangers using paper, string, and twelve tokens. Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Setup  
Six players sit in a circle. Each receives two tokens. A single loop of string is placed in the center; twelve tokens start beside it.

Turn order  
Players take turns clockwise. On your turn, tie one of your tokens to the string with a simple knot, then pass the string to the player on your left.

Shared objective  
Create one continuous string sculpture that uses every token and can be lifted off the table by any two adjacent players without any token touching the surface.

End condition  
The game ends when all twelve tokens are knotted and the sculpture holds steady for a silent count of ten.

Possible failure  
If the sculpture collapses during the count, the group loses.

Recovery rule  
Any player may spend their next turn untying and re-knotting one token to restore balance; the count restarts afterward.

readout.retrieval_query: Design an original cooperative game for six strangers using paper, string, and twelve tokens. Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Setup  
Six players sit in a circle. Each receives two tokens. A single loop of string is placed in the center; twelve tokens start beside it.

Turn order  
Players take turns clockwise. On your turn, move one of your tokens onto the string or slide an existing token one finger-width along it. Then pass the turn.

Shared objective  
Form a single closed loop of tokens on the string so every token touches two others and the loop uses all twelve tokens.

End condition  
The loop is complete when the last gap is closed and every token has exactly two neighbors.

Possible failure  
If three consecutive turns pass with no token moved onto the string, the game ends unfinished.

Recovery rule  
Any player may spend their turn returning one stray token to the center pile instead of moving; this resets the “three-turn” failure counter.

readout.retrieval_query: Design an original cooperative game for six strangers using paper, string, and twelve tokens. Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Setup  
Six players sit in a circle. Each receives two tokens. A single loop of string lies in the center; twelve tokens start beside it.

Turn order  
Players take turns clockwise. On your turn, place one token on the string or move one already on it one finger-width along the loop. You may also pass your second token to any neighbor.

Shared objective  
Fill every space on the string with tokens so the loop is completely covered without gaps or overlaps.

End condition  
The game ends when the string is fully covered or when no tokens remain off the string.

Possible failure  
If three consecutive players cannot place or move a token without creating a gap or overlap, the loop “breaks” and the game ends in failure.

Recovery rule  
Any player may spend both of their tokens to “knot” the string: they remove two adjacent tokens, tie a small overhand knot in that spot, and replace one token on either side of the knot. Play then resumes.

readout.retrieval_query: Design an original cooperative game for six strangers using paper, string, and twelve tokens. Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Setup  
Six players sit in a circle. Each receives two tokens. A single loop of string lies in the center; twelve tokens start beside it.

Turn order  
On your turn, place one token on the string or move one already on it one hand-span clockwise. Then pass the string to the player on your left.

Shared objective  
Create one closed loop of string that carries exactly twelve tokens.

End condition  
The loop is closed and holds twelve tokens; everyone has placed both of their tokens.

Possible failure  
If any player runs out of tokens before twelve are on the string, the game ends unfinished.

Recovery rule  
Any player may give one of their remaining tokens to a neighbor who has none, once per game.

readout.retrieval_query: Design an original cooperative game for six strangers using paper, string, and twelve tokens. Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Setup  
Six players sit in a circle. Each receives two tokens. A single loop of string lies in the center; twelve tokens start beside it.

Turn order  
Players take turns clockwise. On your turn, place one token on the string or move one already on it one hand-span along the loop. You may also pass your second token to any neighbor.

Shared objective  
Form a closed “chain” of exactly twelve tokens spaced evenly around the string. When the chain is complete, all players win.

End condition  
The game ends when either the chain is finished or any player has no tokens left.

Possible failure  
If tokens run out before the chain closes, the group loses.

Recovery rule  
Any player may, once per game, return one token they hold to the supply if doing so lets the next player complete the chain.

readout.retrieval_query: Design an original cooperative game for six strangers using paper, string, and twelve tokens. Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Setup  
Six players sit in a circle. Each receives two tokens. A single loop of string is placed in the center; twelve tokens start beside it.

Turn order  
Players take turns clockwise. On your turn, tie one new knot in the string or move one token from the pile onto an existing knot.

Shared objective  
Weave the string into a single closed net that can hold all twelve tokens without any falling through.

End condition  
The game ends when every token rests on a knot and the string forms a closed loop (ends tied together).

Possible failure  
If three consecutive turns pass with no new knot added and at least one token still off the string, the net collapses and the group loses.

Recovery rule  
Any player may, once per game on their turn, spend both of their tokens to untie one existing knot, returning those tokens to the pile and allowing construction to resume.

readout.retrieval_query: Design an original cooperative game for six strangers using paper, string, and twelve tokens. Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Setup  
Six players sit in a circle. Each receives two tokens. A single loop of string is placed in the center; the twelve tokens start beside it.

Turn order  
Players take turns clockwise. On your turn, place one token on the string or move one already on it one finger-width along the loop. You must also speak one true sentence about yourself that the group has not yet heard.

Shared objective  
Fill the entire loop with tokens so they touch without gaps.

End condition  
The loop is completely covered or every player has used both tokens—whichever happens first.

Possible failure  
If any gap remains after all tokens are placed, the group fails.

Recovery rule  
Any player may spend their turn removing one token from the loop and returning it to the supply, but they must then share a difficulty they overcame; the removed token may be replayed on a later turn.

readout.retrieval_query: Design an original cooperative game for six strangers using paper, string, and twelve tokens. Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Setup  
Six players sit in a circle. Each receives two tokens. A single loop of string lies in the center; twelve tokens start beside it.

Turn order  
Players take turns clockwise. On your turn, place one token on the string or move one already on it one hand-span along the loop. You may also pass your second token to any neighbor.

Shared objective  
Move all twelve tokens once around the loop and back to the start pile using only cooperative placements.

End condition  
The game ends when every token has completed a full circuit and returned, or when no tokens remain on the string and it is a player’s turn with none left to place.

Possible failure  
If the circle breaks (string pulled taut by two opposing pulls) all tokens on the string fall off and are removed from play.

Recovery rule  
Any player may spend both tokens in one turn to retie a broken string, returning one fallen token to the center pile.
